content:
The reference says the session is for planners whose marketing foundations already work and who want to amplify that with ads, which expand reach, reinforce positioning, and attract aligned clients at scale. Ads build on what's already working. They don't replace it.

Candidate A matches this closely. It says "If you've built a planning business you're proud of and want to explore how paid ads can build on the marketing you already do well." It also positions WIA and ads explicitly. Its opening about couples choosing planners is a bit generic, but the substance fits.

Candidate B frames the problem as an unpredictable inbox, with referrals and Instagram doing the heavy lifting. It never mentions ads or WIA, and "not another marketing job" is a different angle. It implies the planner's marketing is lacking ("needs a clearer strategy"), which contradicts the reference's premise that foundations are already dialed in. It also leaves out what the session actually teaches.

A needs fewer edits.

```json
{"winner": "A", "edits_needed_A": "few", "edits_needed_B": "many", "reason": "Candidate A reflects the reference's core message: paid ads build on marketing foundations that already work, with WIA positioned explicitly. Candidate B never mentions ads and frames the planner's marketing as lacking, which cuts against the reference's premise."}
```

request.system:
You compare two draft pieces of marketing copy for Wedding Industry Ads (WIA), a wedding-industry advertising agency. You are given the request, the version WIA's co-founder Whitney actually approved or wrote (the reference), and two candidate drafts. Decide which candidate would need fewer and smaller edits to become something Whitney would approve. Judge substance first (what is claimed, for whom, how WIA is positioned, accuracy, whether her own wording was kept where she supplied it), then voice. Do not reward length, and do not require the candidate to copy the reference wording.

Return only JSON: {"winner": "A" or "B" or "tie", "edits_needed_A": "few", "edits_needed_B": "many", "reason": "one or two sentences"} where edits_needed values are none, few, some or many.

Request:
I need another email for the morning of my session. Here's a template the summit host provided, but it's pretty generic

Suggested subject line: Join me today to learn about [presentation topic]

Alt Subject line: My session is live — here’s why it matters

 

Hey [Name],

I wanted to personally let you know that my session for the 2026 Planners Workshop is now available.

I’m teaching [SESSION TITLE], and I created it because I keep seeing planners struggle with [INSERT PROBLEM YOU SEE OFTEN].

In this session, we’ll cover:

[Talking point 1]





[Talking point 2]





[Talking point 3]





My goal is simple: to help you [INSERT CLEAR OUTCOME] so you can book better weddings and feel more confident doing it.

If you haven’t registered yet, you can still grab a free ticket here:

 [YOUR AFFILIATE LINK]

I’d love for you to watch it,

 [Your name]

Reference (what Whitney approved):
I created this session for planners who are ready to amplify what’s already working in their business.

When your marketing foundations are dialed in, ads become a strategic way to expand reach, reinforce positioning, and attract more aligned clients at scale.

Candidate A:
Subject: Your next couples are still choosing their planner
Preview text: My session at the 2026 Planners Workshop is available today.

Hey [Name],

Couples have a lot to consider when choosing a wedding planner. Your portfolio helps them picture the day. Your approach helps them imagine what it would feel like to work with you.

Good advertising gives more of the right couples the opportunity to see both.

At Wedding Industry Ads, we think about that connection long before a campaign goes live. Who are we trying to reach? What matters to them? And what would give them the confidence to inquire?

That’s the perspective I’m bringing to my session at the **2026 Planners Workshop**, **[SESSION TITLE]**, which is available today.

If you’ve built a planning business you’re proud of and want to explore how paid ads can build on the marketing you already do well, I’d love for you to join me.

You can still register for free and watch here:

[YOUR AFFILIATE LINK]

And if you watch, reply and tell me what stood out. I’d love to hear what it brought up for your business.

Whitney

Candidate B:
Subject: A strong reputation. An unpredictable inbox.

Hey [Name],

You can be an excellent planner, deliver a thoughtful client experience, and have a portfolio you’re proud of—and still wonder where your next inquiry is coming from.

That doesn’t mean you need to work harder at being visible.

It may mean your marketing needs a clearer strategy, not more of your time.

When referrals and Instagram do most of the heavy lifting, it’s easy to feel like every quiet week requires you to do something more. Post more. Network more. Find another way to stay in front of people.

But the goal isn’t to give yourself another marketing job. It’s to build a business that keeps creating opportunities while you’re taking care of your couples.

If that’s the kind of growth you’re thinking about, I’d love for you to join me today.

My session, **[SESSION TITLE]**, is now available inside the **2026 Planners Workshop**.

You can still register for free and watch here:

**[Grab your free ticket → YOUR AFFILIATE LINK]**

Hope to see you there,

Whitney
